source.title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; no apparent cut-off or garbling that prevents extracting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests whether representations can be functionally transferred by a linear stitch and argues that geometric similarity and functional interchangeability are distinct. It refines the convergence claim by showing both substantial transfer in some settings and large, metric- and task-dependent gaps.
record.gate_note: The study reports model-stitching results, cross-representation geometry, and tagging performance that bear on representation transfer and metric dependence. Its node-masking ablations concern which inputs a trained tagger uses, rather than the listed convergence versions, so they are not included as rows. The paper also reports a hypergraph comparison, included below because it tests whether a different reader recovers information from the same representation.
record.test_reason: The study trains a linear stitch between two independently trained transformers that share an architecture but read different inputs (particles vs Lund splittings). It measures how much function survives the map, which bears on V4. It also shows that AUC and CKA/SVCCA suggest interchangeability that background rejection does not, and argues explicitly that geometric similarity is not functional interchangeability, which bears on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the primary Lund branch's deficit is representational: ParT's frozen downstream reads it at least as well as its own does, yet stays far below ParT. The deficit is invisible in AUC and in rising CKA, which do not track functional transfer. The full declustering tree repairs 72% of the gap on top tagging, though the trained network relies at inference mostly on primary nodes. On quark/gluon tagging the primary branch already retains 77.6% of ParT and the tree closes only 33%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses class-token model stitching and downstream task performance rather than directly comparing representation distances as in the cited similarity methods. It matches the ParT backbone across input representations and trains a single linear bridge; it does not test the original sources' scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The conclusion depends strongly on metric: AUC retention is near 1 while background rejection reveals large gaps. CKA rises with depth without tracking functional transfer. Results also differ between top and quark/gluon tagging, and shallow-depth quark/gluon stitches have large seed spread.

fits_no_version.finding: A hypergraph reader and a pairwise-attention reader trained separately on the same primary-branch input reach the same rejection (116 vs 112±7). The study reads this as information content being reader-independent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different architectures trained on the same input extract similar task-relevant information (functional equivalence without a representation mapping).

record.code_released: Available from the authors on reasonable request
record.problems: Five seeds are used; the authors call the consumer-asymmetry test underpowered (p = 0.062). The quark/gluon shallow-depth stitch results have 20–55% relative seed spreads and are explicitly described as unresolved. The hypergraph comparison uses one seed and 10% of the dataset. The stitch injects a single-token sequence into the target; the paper uses self-stitch controls to assess the associated cost. Depth 6 is excluded from the stitch sweep on structural grounds.
record.rows_left_out: The quark/gluon CKA and SVCCA endpoint values in Table XI are not separately rowed; the row cap was used for the full set of primary-branch stitching conditions, controls, and top-tagging geometric measurements. The hypergraph particle-input comparison in Table VI is also omitted because it tests a different input representation rather than transfer between the Lund representations. Node-masking and primary-step ablations in Sections VI–VII and Appendix A are not convergence-version results.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability; depth indexes layers within fixed models.
Seeds are only averaged over; features shared across seeds are not measured.

Tests only a learned linear class-token stitch. Relative representations, mapping without paired data, and other stitch interfaces are not tested. The two models share an architecture and training data and differ only in input representation.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits are compared across models.
Neighbour-count or kernel settings of similarity measures are not swept; no out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of a plateau or of shared data or objectives as the cause. CKA reaches 0.93–0.96, and the functional gap is attributed to information missing from one input, not to incomplete convergence.

missing.what: Quark/gluon source-normalized retained rejection for all four stitch conditions (e.g. lund→part 0.494→0.983, part→lund 0.524→0.918) and retained AUC by depth
Quark/gluon CKA/SVCCA: full tree starts lower (CKA 0.379 vs 0.639 at d=1) but ends higher at d=6 (0.919 vs 0.884)
Top-tagging full-tree CKA rising from 0.747 to 0.960 (d=1 to 5); primary-branch CKA at d=6 is 0.935
d=6 stitches with a Lund-ParT target lose about half their rejection while AUC moves under 0.005; the authors exclude this depth
Rejection at εS=0.3 for all stitch conditions

record.verdict_notes: Same architecture, same data and same objective, with only the input representation differing, so this is a weak test of convergence across different architectures or objectives. The source-normalized metric is the relevant one for V4 interchangeability. Self-stitch controls show that stitch losses at shallow depth come largely from injecting a single token, so cross-model losses should be read against them. V7 is moved to untested.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability; depth indexes layers within fixed-size models.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
Five training seeds are used for averaging, but the study does not measure shared features or subspaces across independently initialized models of the same architecture.
Tests a single learned linear map at a class-token stitch point. It does not test relative representations, stitching at other kinds of layer interfaces, or mapping without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.
Tests AUC, background rejection at specified signal efficiencies, linear CKA, and SVCCA. Does not sweep similarity-measure settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.

Shows incomplete functional transfer and metric-dependent geometric alignment. It does not causally test whether shared training data or objectives explain the alignment, and does not test a scale-dependent plateau.

relationships.display_finding: Linear stitches retained 0.942–0.998 of source rejection and exceeded lund-self, with full-tree rejection 242 versus 248 and quark/gluon retention approximately 0.98.

relationships.condition: ParT source into Lund-ParT, and shallow stitch depths on both tasks
relationships.reason: Retained rejection is 0.20–0.91 (A22–A38 cross rows), 0.54 for the full tree at d=1 (D01), and 0.49–0.82 for noisy quark/gluon shallow depths (B01–B07). Losses roughly match self-stitch, so they reflect the injection method, not only mismatch.
relationships.display_finding: Retained rejection ranged from 0.20–0.91 across models, reached 0.54 for the full tree at depth 1, and ranged from 0.49–0.82 at noisy shallow quark/gluon depths; similar losses when stitching models to themselves implicated the injection method.
